## Observations

1. The input consists of one line containing the string S.
2. S is guaranteed to be nonempty, and only its first character is needed.
3. The output is the first character of S followed immediately by the literal uppercase suffix UPC.

## Solution sketch

> The input consists of one line containing the string S.

1. Read the line from standard input. For a string of length n, reading and storing it takes O(n) time and O(n) space.

> S is guaranteed to be nonempty, and only its first character is needed.

2. Take the first character and ignore the rest. This also works when S has length one, so no special case is needed.

> The output is the first character of S followed immediately by the literal uppercase suffix UPC.

3. Append UPC to the selected character and print the resulting four-character string on its own line. Selecting the character and producing the output take O(1) time and O(1) extra space beyond the stored input.
